searches.outcome: Found the Open Library record and alternate lecture-note treatments; the candidate MIT 18.226 PDF redirected to an inaccessible host, while the already-stamped Sullivan lecture notes cover the required binomial expectation.

searches.query: Bernstein polynomial Lipschitz approximation error lecture notes binomial variance full proof pdf
searches.outcome: Found lecture-note explanations of the Bernstein expectation and variance argument; Sullivan §5.1 was already fetched as full text and read.

alternatives.argument: The local proof writes the Bernstein polynomial as E[f(S/N)] for S a sum of N independent Bernoulli(x) variables, applies the Lipschitz bound, Cauchy–Schwarz, Var(S)=Nx(1−x), and x(1−x)≤1/4. This proves the uniform L/(2√N) estimate without importing the inaccessible book.

The local counterexample uses the complete Bernstein estimate proved in lem-bernstein-polynomial-lipschitz-error: the 32-Lipschitz target h^5 has a degree-2^22 polynomial within 1/128 uniformly. The polynomial is an allowed single (1,1,2^22)-semi-algebraic gate using the constant predicate q_1=1 with condition q_1>=0, contradicting the 1/64 claim.
